decision: Retain compositional live reporting; a separate materialized reporting read model is not justified by the measured DEV-16 bottlenecks.
basis: All four captured expensive query shapes now seek the new narrow indexes; the paged time list no longer sorts before TOP.
Read/write/search p95 passed in the first after-index 50-session run and the final guarded rerun.
No cross-module reporting schema or new consistency lag is required to achieve the observed improvement.
The active first after-index window processed 2.629x HTTP requests; approximate Web allocated bytes per request remained approximately stable (570→567 KiB process-wide).
limitations: These are sequential synthetic local runs on a shared M4 laptop with emulated SQL and a 2 GiB engine target; EXT-05 capacity acceptance remains separate.

Baseline cache counters and after-index post-two-run counters have different execution counts/lifetimes; per-execution averages and plan access paths support the diagnosis, not an isolated controlled benchmark.
After-index full runtime capture contains part of the second guard run; active-window comparison is in resource-comparison.json.
Index write/storage overhead is not isolated by this experiment, although workload write p95 improved and migration kept existing records/financial totals.
reconsiderWhen: If agreed-environment measurements still breach read/reporting SLO under representative concurrency after these indexes, profile the remaining exact query shapes.
If repeated full-history BI/report aggregates dominate measured CPU/IO, evaluate an explicit reporting projection with agreed freshness, reconciliation, ownership and an ADR.
